answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to claim a unique physical lantern whose optical signature is calibrated at a trusted oasis of measurement labs. The lantern emits a one-time nebula of entangled photons that the network verifies against a public commitment; cloning the hardware costs the attacker the full fabrication expense of a new device plus the irreversible loss of the original's quantum state. This raises the marginal cost of each fake identity above any expected reward from flooding the network.
